chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Attar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Seek knowledge and adorn yourselves along with it with forbearance and dignity, and be humble toward those you teach knowledge to, and be humble toward those from whom you sought knowledge, and do not become tyrannical scholars such that your falsehoods obliterate your truth.

key_terms.الباطل: Falsehood, the void — that which is inherently wrong or vain
key_terms.التواضع: Humility, lowliness — a cardinal virtue in Islamic ethics, here applied bidirectionally to teacher and student
key_terms.الحق: Truth, right — that which is established and real
key_terms.الحِلم: Forbearance, clemency — the capacity to remain composed and gentle even when provoked
key_terms.الوقار: Dignity, gravity, gravitas — the composed and measured bearing befitting a person of knowledge
key_terms.عُلَماء جَبَّارون: Tyrannical scholars — scholars who exploit religious authority for coercion or arrogance, the antithesis of the scholar's proper role

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the character and humility required of Islamic scholars?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a threefold exhortation to scholars: pursue knowledge actively, embody the virtues of forbearance (hilm) and gravity (waqar) as its inseparable companions, and maintain humility toward both students and teachers alike. The warning against becoming 'tyrannical scholars' (ulama' jabbarun) reflects the Imam's concern that religious authority, when untempered by humility, can corrupt the very truth it claims to uphold, causing one's errors to negate one's genuine contributions.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya Al Attar, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Seek the knowledge and adorn (yourselves) along with it, with the forbearance, and the dignity, and the humbleness towards the ones whom you teach it to, and humbleness towards the one whom you sought the knowledge from, and do not become tyrannous scholars, as your falsehoods would remove your truth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya al-‘Attar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from Mu‘awiya ibn Wahab who has said the following. “Imam abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said.

“Seek knowledge and beautify it with forbearance and dignity. Be humble to your students and to those from whom you learn. Do not be a tyrant scholar lest your falsehood would destroy the truth in you.”
